title: Mass. to be 4th state to roll out EBT chip cards to curb fraud
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Massachusetts will distribute chip-enabled EBT cards to prevent SNAP benefit fraud, following a successful pilot in Worcester.
Nearly 1 million residents use EBT for SNAP benefits. The cards are accepted at about 5,500 retailers across the state.
Recipients can lock their new cards via the DTA Connect app or customer service, enhancing security against scams.

title: Boston is now offering ‘pet certificates’ for couples who wed at City Hall
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Boston City Hall now offers 'pet certificates' for couples who get married there, including their pets in the union.
Mayor Michelle Wu announced the initiative, aiming to officially welcome pets into couples' households with a special certificate.
The certificate, recognized by the 'City of Boston Department of Cuddles', commemorates the couple's commitment to their pets.

title: Kevin Nealon discusses Conan, Dunkin’, SNL and more ahead of local shows
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Kevin Nealon will perform shows in Boston on August 1 and Portsmouth, NH on August 8.
Nealon discusses his comedic evolution, using Twitter and YouTube to engage audiences ahead of his special 'Loose in the Crotch.'
Former SNL cast member shares experiences from 'Hiking with Kevin' and collaborations with Adam Sandler.

title: Red Sox’ Willson Contreras leaves game after scary HBP vs. Dodgers
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox's Willson Contreras hit in the head by a 95 MPH pitch from Dodgers pitcher Will Klein.
Contreras initially remained in the game but was replaced defensively in the next half-inning.
Contreras leads the Red Sox in batting average, on-base percentage, and several other offensive categories this season.

title: After Patriots coaching stint, DeAndre Hopkins joins Georgia Tech staff
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: DeAndre Hopkins joins Georgia Tech as an assistant wide receivers coach after New England Patriots training camp.
Hopkins attended Patriots camp weighing his options to continue playing or transition to coaching.
Hopkins connects with Georgia Tech's coach, thanks to his familiarity with the ACC and previous NFL experience.

title: Could Efton Chism and Kyle Williams both make the Patriots 53-man roster?
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: The Patriots face a surplus of talent in their wide receiver corps, with seven players vying for typical six roster spots.
Efton Chism and Kyle Williams both impressed in training camp, enhancing their chances to make the 53-man roster.
Receiver decisions are complicated by Kayshon Boutte's potential trade and Mack Hollins' leadership role in the group.

title: Reports: OF George Springer interested in trade to Red Sox, team eyeing INF Xavier Edwards
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: George Springer of the Blue Jays shows interest in a trade to the Red Sox before the deadline.
Red Sox are considering trading for Marlins infielder Xavier Edwards, per Ken Rosenthal's report.
Springer has a strong hitting record at Fenway and would permit a trade to Boston, says CBS Sports.

title: 5 must-watch movies & TV shows streaming right now
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' is now streaming on Hulu, reuniting Meryl Streep and Anne Hathaway with a story on media woes.
'The Drama' starring Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, a dark comedy on cancel culture, is available on HBO Max.
'Furious' Season 1, featuring Emmy Rossum as an FBI rookie, is streaming on Hulu and brings a crime thriller narrative.

title: Here’s how home, away broadcasts reacted to Jarren Duran’s on-field flare-up
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Jarren Duran's on-field outburst against teammate Willson Contreras and coach Chad Epperson drew reactions from NESN and WEEI broadcasts.
Broadcasters across different networks criticized Duran for showing frustration over a non-scoring play during the Red Sox versus Athletics game.
The Red Sox are reportedly open to trading Duran ahead of the MLB trade deadline, following the incident.

title: Drake Maye on building chemistry with A.J. Brown: ‘I am not going to shy away from him.’
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Drake Maye and A.J. Brown are developing strong chemistry during New England Patriots training camp.
Brown and Maye connected for multiple completions during recent practices, indicating improved coordination.
Maye emphasized aggressive play, continually involving Brown to enhance their on-field connection.
